Game.Overview: Zettai Zetsumei Dangerous Jiisan: Naki no Ikkai is an Action game, developed by Rokumendo and published by Kids Station, which was released in Japan in 2004.

Game.Name: Zettaizetsumei Dangerous Jiisan: Shijou Saikyou no Dogeza
Game.Overview: Zettai Zetsumei Dangerous Jiisan: Shijou Saikyou no Dogeza is an Action game, developed by Rokumendo and published by Kids Station, which was released in Japan in 2003.

Game.Name: Zettaizetsumei Dangerous Jiisan Tsuu: Ikari no Oshioki Blues
Game.Overview: Zettai Zetsumei Dangerous Jiisan Tsuu: Ikari no Oshioki Blues is an Adventure game, developed by Rokumendo and published by Kids Station, which was released in Japan in 2004.

Game.Name: Zidane: Football Generation 2002
Game.Overview:
Zidane: Football Generation 2002 is a football game, developed by Aqua Pacific and published by Cryo Interactive, which was released in Europe in 2002.
Find Zidane right at the heart of world football : 75 national teams, 3 game modes including one exclusive free kick challenge, spectacular animation and unequalled playability, that's what makes up the official game of the world number one footballer : Zidane.

Game.Name: Zipline Zapper
Game.Overview:
I'm excited to share my 3D Game Boy Advance game with you!
Ride the zipline through the beautiful detailed and textured 3D environments while aiming your zapper at the targets to gain points. The outer purple is worth 2 points while the center yellow is worth 5 points. After completing the 3 levels, you will see your score out of the total possible 160.
Press the up button during the title sequence to increase the zipline speed. A red dot in the lower left corner lets you know that level has been set to hard mode.
Press the down arrow during the title sequence to lower the zipline speed for that level. You might find this helpful!
A button fires the zapper
B button jump when you are on the ground
Left shoulder button look down
Right shoulder button look up
This runs on a GBA emulator like mGBA or on a flashcart on the actual hardware!
I hope to further develop my game with your feedback. Add more and have Zipline Zapper published on an actual GBA cartridge with box art! And it will include the level editor I also programmed that runs on the GBA. So all you need is the ROM and you can design your own levels.
I want to also make a tutorial video explaining how I was able to program such optimized C code to push this much 3D detail on the old Game Boy Advance.
I programmed this completely from scratch, it's all my own code, no libraries, no AI, it's just me!

Game.Name: Zoey 101
Game.Overview: Zoey 101 is an Adventure game, developed by Barking Lizards and published by THQ, which was released in 2007.

Game.Name: Zoids: Legacy
Game.Overview: At the outer reaches of the universe, the human inhabitants on the Planet Zi remain locked in combat. The population, divided between good and evil, uses gargantuan life forms called Zoids to battle each other for control of this world. During a recent weapons experiment, Planet Zi underwent an accidental time-space fusion, creating a collision of Zoids warriors from two eras, the Chaotic Century and the New Century. Now, all hopes of returning Planet Zi to normal rest with Zeru, a promising Zoids warrior. Help Van, Fiona, Bit Cloud and Zeru use the full power of the ZOIDS to bring peace to their world. As the story unfolds, players can customize and upgrade their own unique Zoids to improve its efficiency and perform combination attack moves. Released in Japan as Zoids Saga II, Legacy features more than 140 different types of Zoids, each can be customized with different weapons and new color schemes.

Game.Name: Zoids Saga
Game.Overview: Zoids Saga is a Role-Playing game, developed by Amedio and published by Tomy Corporation, which was released in Japan in 2001.

Game.Name: Zoids Saga: Fuzors
Game.Overview: Zoids Saga: Fuzors is a Role-Playing game, developed by Amedio and published by Tomy Corporation, which was released in Japan in 2004.

Game.Name: Zone of the Enders: The Fist of Mars
Game.Overview:
In the distant future, mankind is at the brink of war with it's colonies on the moon, Mars and Jupiter. You take control of a young man who, after a series of events, finds himself in possession of a new type of L.E.V. (a giant combat robot) and stranded on Mars, where he joins forces with the Anti-Terrestrial League.
Zone of the Enders: The Fist of Mars is a side-story in the Zone of the Enders series. The gameplay alternates between story sequences and tactical turn-based combat, in which the player controls a number of L.E.V.s on a square grid map. There are different types of L.E.V.s that differ in speed, durability, movement range and armament. Unlike close ranged weapons, long range weapons cannot be used after an L.E.V. has already been moved. When two units engage in combat, the I.A.S. (interactive action system) comes into play. When attacking, the player is given a limited amount of time to move a cross-hair over your target. Critical hits can be delivered by successfully aiming at certain weak-spots of your enemies. When attacked by an enemy, the player must try to keep his/her own target icon away from the enemy's. The IAS can be toggled on and off in the options menu.
At the end of each chapter the player is able to upgrade the controlled L.E.V.s or equip them with certain items that can sometimes be found during missions. The "balance" sub-screen allows to determine whether an L.E.V. should focus on attack power or accuracy, evasion or minimizing damage.

Game.Name: ZooCube
Game.Overview: Created by PuzzleKings, ZooCube takes puzzlers to a whole new dimension - the third dimension. Around the world, animals have been transformed by shape-altering science experiments and need help in returning to their natural state. Players use their ZooCube to rescue and return the animals to the flying ark.

Game.Name: Zooo: Action Puzzle Game
Game.Overview: Zooo: Action Puzzle Game is a Puzzle game, developed by Buddiez, Inc. and published by Success, which was released in Japan in 2003. US version cancelled, released in Europe and Japan in 2005.

Platform.Name: Nintendo Game Boy Advance
Platform.Cpu: ARM7TDMI @16.78 MHz and Sharp LR35902 @ 4.19 MHz
Platform.Memory: 32 KB + 96 KB VRAM (CPU), 256 KB DRAM (ex CPU)
Platform.Sound: Dual 8-bit DAC plus all Gameboy legacy channels
Platform.Notes: The Game Boy Advance (abbreviated as GBA) is a 32-bit handheld video game console developed, manufactured and marketed by Nintendo as the successor to the Game Boy Color. It was released in Japan on March 21, 2001, in North America on June 11, 2001, in Australia and Europe on June 22, 2001, and in mainland China on June 8, 2004 (iQue Player). Nintendo's competitors in the handheld market at the time were the Neo Geo Pocket Color, WonderSwan, GP32, Tapwave Zodiac, and the N-Gage. Despite the competitors' best efforts, Nintendo maintained a majority market share with the Game Boy Advance. As of June 30, 2010, the Game Boy Advance series has sold 81.51 million units worldwide. Its successor, the Nintendo DS, was released in November 2004 and is also compatible with Game Boy Advance software.

GameAlternateName.AlternateName: Famicom Mini 25: The Legend of Zelda 2: Link no Bouken
NES Classics: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
